preamble: In the Vhe (Ewe) dialects of Gbe, the back fricatives became the bilabial fricatives [ɸ] and [β], which Ewe writes ⟨ƒ⟩ and ⟨ʋ⟩. Capo reconstructs labialized back fricatives *χʷ and *ʁʷ for Proto-Gbe. Fon, Ajá and Phla-Pherá keep them as [xʷ] (Fon ⟨xw⟩, which is velar) or as plain [x] before rounded vowels, while Vhe changed them to [ɸ] and [β]. The lip rounding of the source became the main place of articulation and the back constriction was lost. Capo argues that the Ewe bilabial fricatives, a well-known contrast with [f] and [v], are a Vhe innovation and were not inherited from Proto-Gbe.
phoneticEffects: Labialization, Fronting, Loss Of Dorsal Articulation
